author: Nelev
body:
## Summary

The greeting said "Hi Mattia" to every user. The page-load preview (`GET /`) ignored the name it was given, and `POST /ask` seeded the stored greeting with the same literal. Both now use the signed-in user's Clerk first name and share one fallback ("Hi there").

- **UI:** `greetingName()` (`api/session.ts`) reads the first name with Clerk's `currentUser()`. The page sends it to `GET /`. `ask()` sends it to `POST /ask` only when starting a conversation, so later messages make no Clerk call.
- **API:** `POST /ask` takes an optional `user` query parameter for the seeded greeting. Both routes share one `GreetingName` type (1–200 characters) and one default, `"there"`. Ownership still comes only from the session token.
- **Cleanup:** the chat-header patient badge is removed. It showed a hardcoded record id, not the signed-in patient. The `.pulse-dot` styles it used are removed too.

## Contract changes

- `GET /` with no `user` now returns "Hi there" instead of a 422.
- `GET /` now rejects an empty or over-200-character `user` with a 422, the same as `POST /ask`.
- The README API table and notes are updated.

## Not in this PR

Each page load now waits on a Clerk Backend API call (`currentUser()`) before the greeting fetch. A simpler design would resolve the name inside the API, from a `firstName` claim on the session token. That removes the `user` parameter and the extra call, but needs the claim added in the Clerk dashboard first.

## Test plan

- [x] API: `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `pytest` (119 passed)
- [x] UI: `format:check`, `tsc --noEmit`, `lint`, `vitest` (36 passed)
- [ ] Manual: sign in with an account that has a first name and check that the preview and the stored greeting both use it
